title: Discovery Redirected the Customer to a Better-Fit Architecture
shortSummary: A customer initially requested a feature in one product, but discovery revealed that their real problem was scale and isolation. The SA declined to promise an unsupported roadmap change and redirected the conversation toward a better-fit architecture, which the customer then chose to evaluate.
situation: A high-volume customer asked for a feature that the current product did not support on their timeline.
task: Understand the underlying outcome, determine whether the requested feature was actually the right solution, and recommend a supportable path without overselling the roadmap.
actions: Asked why the requested feature mattered rather than treating it as the requirement.
Mapped the customer's scale, workload, timeline, and isolation needs.
Recognized that an adjacent architecture better fit the underlying problem.
Explained the limitation candidly and proposed the alternate path despite initial resistance.
Connected the customer to the relevant Product team after they chose to explore the alternative.
results: The customer moved from requesting an unsupported feature to evaluating a better-fit architecture.
The SA preserved trust by avoiding a roadmap promise that could not be supported.
Exact commercial outcome remains to verify.
